meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.name: PXR (NR1I2)
data.description: Pregnane X receptor, a xenobiotic-sensing nuclear receptor whose activation drives liver growth via the AKT-mTOR pathway.
data.description_beginner: A sensor in liver cells that detects foreign chemicals and drugs and switches on the genes needed to break them down. Turning it on also makes the liver grow, and that growth instruction is carried by the AKT-mTOR pathway.

studies.title: Pregnane X receptor-mediated liver growth: a controlled clinical trial in healthy volunteers and identification of the role of AKT-MTOR pathway in mouse.
studies.authors: Lassila P; Karpale M; Kummu O et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human controlled clinical trial (n=16); mouse (PXR-humanised, PCN)
studies.finding: One week of rifampicin increased the liver volume-to-body-weight ratio by 2.7% in 16 healthy volunteers, and PXR activation enlarged the liver in male mice, accompanied by increased AKT-MTOR pathway activity, without YAP activation.
